missions.title: Lights Out on the Rim
missions.text: A tired woman in a Concord warden's coat is nursing the cheapest tea the bar sells. A lantern at Skerry went dark last week, and nobody can say why. She needs a pilot who will look at it without writing a report about how brave they were.
missions.acceptText: Corrin slides a scanner key across the table and finishes the tea like it owed her money. Skerry is a long way out, so go with a full tank. She would like to hear what the lantern has to say.

steps.text: Fly to Skerry and scan the dead lantern.

onComplete.text: The Skerry lantern was not worn out. Its core is simply gone. Warden Corrin wants a second opinion from someone who reads dead cores.
The lantern's housing is open and its core is gone. A fragment of the cut edge is yours to carry. Corrin pays you 3,000 cr.

missions.title: A Second Opinion
missions.text: Corrin has been through the Skerry scans a dozen times and trusts none of them. She wants the core fragment in front of Odo Haskett, an analyst at Lastlight who can read a dead core like a letter. He is slow, honest, and not cheap. She needs him within eight days.
missions.acceptText: A one-ton crate of fragment and packing is sealed and strapped to your hold. Corrin writes Haskett's name on it twice, in case you forget. Lastlight is where he keeps his instruments, and his opinions.

steps.text: Deliver the core fragment to Odo Haskett at Lastlight within 8 days.

onComplete.text: Haskett says the Skerry core was cut out with a proper tool, not burned out. Someone is taking lantern cores on purpose.
Haskett turns the fragment over twice and says one word, quietly: cut. He pays you 4,000 cr from Corrin's purse.

missions.title: Low Tide
missions.text: Haskett has drawn a faint line on a napkin, from the cut edge of your fragment to a scavenger ship called the Low Tide. Its captain, Mags Orrin, buys what falls off other people's lanterns and knows where it goes. She is currently parked at Brackwater and enjoys being asked nicely.
missions.acceptText: Haskett taps the napkin and tells you to bring food, money, or a very good face. Brackwater is only a couple of jumps off the main lanes. The Low Tide will be easy to spot, being the ship that looks like it is hiding.

steps.text: Find the Low Tide at Brackwater and talk to Mags Orrin.

card.title: The Low Tide
card.text: Mags Orrin's voice crackles over the channel, cheerful and unhurried. She knows where the cores go, and she knows what an answer is worth. Her price comes in three flavours, none of them free.

outcomes.text: Mags counts the credits twice and sends a bearing: a hidden lane out of Oxbow, deep into the dark.
Ten tons of food go across, and Mags sends a bearing with a happy sigh. Her crew have been eating tinned beans for weeks.
You mention the cargo in your hold, as if it were a prelude to something. Mags squints, laughs, and sends the bearing anyway.

onComplete.text: The Low Tide gave a bearing for a hidden lane from Oxbow into the Dimming. The first system out there is called Gloam.
The lane from Oxbow into the Dimming is now on your chart. Gloam is the first port of call.

missions.combatLater: A fight with the Low Tide if the bluff fails.

missions.title: Past the Charts
missions.text: A calm voice comes over the channel as you cross out of the charts. This is Ama Reed, speaker for the Unlit Holdings, and she knows exactly why you are here. Someone is stripping the old lanterns just beyond Gloam, and she would rather you saw it for yourself than heard it from a Concord report.
missions.acceptText: Reed marks a stripped-lantern field on your chart and wishes you luck, in the voice of someone who has said it too often. A man named Bram Kettle is working there, and he is not a villain. Be ready for his crew to be less polite.

steps.text: Make your way into Gloam, past the edge of the charts.
Search Gloam for the stripped lantern field.
Talk to Bram Kettle and decide what to do with what you know.

card.title: Bram Kettle
card.text: Bram Kettle is tired, thin, and not hiding a thing. His crew were never paid by the Concord, so they took what the Concord left to rot. You hold the evidence and the lane charts, and either could end him. One of them could end the lanterns going dark.

outcomes.text: You chose the Concord. Warden Corrin is waiting at Concordance with a charter and a pen.
The evidence goes to the Concord. Corrin pays 6,000 cr and asks you to come to Concordance.
You chose the Free Reach. Tamsin Vey is waiting at Wrenhold with a contract she will keep to the letter.
The charts go to the Free Reach. Vey pays 6,000 cr and invites you to Wrenhold.

missions.title: The Missing Courier
missions.text: Hettie Marsh has a ledger with one red line in it. Pell Darrow's courier is nine days overdue on the Vesk run, and Pell is never late. She would like someone to find out whether he is dead, drunk, or merely sulking.
missions.acceptText: Marsh gives you Pell's last known route and a flask of something that is not tea. Start at Vesk and work back through Mirren. She expects good news, but has packed for the other kind.

steps.text: Ask at Vesk Outpost when Pell last passed through.
Search Mirren for Pell Darrow's courier.
Take the news back to Hettie Marsh at Lastlight.

onComplete.text: Pell Darrow swears a ship with no running lights shadowed him off the Brackwater lane, before his drive quit. He thinks it was the Low Tide.
Pell is alive, cross, and short of a drive coil. Marsh pays 5,000 cr and tells you about the unlit ship that scared him.

missions.title: The Surveyor's Charts
missions.text: Isolde Marek has the look of someone who has lost something small and valuable. A surveyor she trained sent two chart tubes in the post and neither arrived. They are somewhere in Thistle and Cinderfall, and she would very much like them back.
missions.acceptText: Marek gives you a beacon key for the first tube and a stern look for the second. The surveyor was careful, so the tubes will not be lying about. When you have both, bring them to her at Corvana.

steps.text: Scan the first chart tube's beacon in Thistle.
Search Cinderfall for the second chart tube.
Bring both tubes back to Isolde Marek at Corvana Works.

onComplete.text: Marek unrolls both tubes and weeps briefly into her sleeve. She says the Surveyor's Folio is yours to buy at the Corvana outfitter. It is a map, and the surveyor would have wanted it used.

missions.title: The Pilgrim Road: First Lamp
missions.text: Oriel Pask leads a small procession of pilgrims who walk, when they can, and fly, when they must. They keep the Four Lamps, a road of shrines at the lit edges of the charts, and the first lamp is at Lastlight Beacon. Three of them cannot manage the stairs, let alone the lanes south.
missions.acceptText: Pask counts out three pilgrims and a bag of lamp-oil, in that order of importance. The way runs south from Minster through Mirren and Vesk to Lastlight. She will pay on arrival and says the Road does not hurry.

steps.text: Ferry the three pilgrims to the first lamp at Lastlight Beacon.

onComplete.text: The keepers of Lastlight light the first lamp and feed the pilgrims soup. Pask pays you 3,000 cr, and asks that you find her again in the bar here. The second lamp waits at Skerry Light.

missions.title: The Pilgrim Road: Second Lamp
missions.text: Pask has rested, and so have the pilgrims, and the soup has done its work. The second lamp is a cold bright station called Skerry Light, at the very rim. She asks if you would take them on.
missions.acceptText: The three pilgrims file back aboard, quieter than before. The way runs from Lastlight through Brackwater to Skerry. They have been told it is cold there and are pleased about it.

steps.text: Ferry the pilgrims to the second lamp at Skerry Light.

onComplete.text: The pilgrims kneel on the heated deck of Skerry Light and the dockhands pretend not to watch. Pask pays you 3,000 cr. She will be in the bar here, and the third lamp is the boarding house at Ferryman's Rest in Oxbow.

missions.title: The Pilgrim Road: Third Lamp
missions.text: Pask has found a seat by the heater and does not intend to give it up for long. The third lamp is Ferryman's Rest, a boarding house in orbit above Oxbow, kept by a pilot who has carried pilgrims for free since before the Reach had a name. She asks whether you will carry them too.
missions.acceptText: The pilgrims pack their shawls and leave a candle burning for the next travellers. The way runs from Skerry through Redwater to Oxbow. Pask says the old pilot will want to hear about the weather.

steps.text: Ferry the pilgrims to the third lamp at Ferryman's Rest.

onComplete.text: The old pilot at Ferryman's Rest takes the pilgrims' bags and tells them about the weather at length. Pask pays you 3,000 cr. The last lamp waits at Hollis Landing, and she will meet you in the bar there.

missions.title: The Pilgrim Road: Last Lamp
missions.text: The pilgrims have walked the length of the charts on other people's engines, and the last lamp is the nearest thing the Road has to a door. It stands at Hollis Landing, the last proper Concord port before the Reach. Pask asks you to see them through.
missions.acceptText: The pilgrims bow to the old pilot and then, slightly less gravely, to you. The way runs from Oxbow through Wrenhold to Hollis. Pask has stopped counting heads and started counting stairs.

steps.text: Ferry the pilgrims to the last lamp at Hollis Landing.

onComplete.text: Pask says the four lamps burn a little brighter when a pilot has carried the pilgrims between them, and that nobody has ever asked her to prove it.
The last lamp is lit and the Road is walked. Pask pays you 3,000 cr, and leaves a note on your pillow that reads only: thank you for the stairs.

missions.title: Two Houses
missions.text: Dill Harrow keeps the peace on the Redwater docks, which means he keeps a list. The Marlow and Teague haulers have fed each other's quarrels for three generations, and this season they cannot agree on who owns a shipment of sluice-valve castings. He would like a pilot with no cousins on either side.
missions.acceptText: Harrow loads five tons of castings and tells you to start at Redwater Locks, where the paperwork lives. After that, you will meet a hauler in Oxbow who has an opinion. Hear them out, pick a house, and bring the castings back to the Sound.

steps.text: Collect the disputed shipping papers at Redwater Locks.
Find the hauler waiting in Oxbow and choose a house.

card.title: Marlow and Teague
card.text: A Marlow hull and a Teague hull sit nose to nose in the shipping lane, each captain on an open channel and neither prepared to be the first to leave. Both have read the papers you are carrying. Both would like you to say, out loud, that they are right.

outcomes.text: Hob Marlow cracks a grin and gives you a salute of one finger. The Teague captain says nothing and cuts the channel. Take the castings back to Redwater Sound.
The Teague captain thanks you with great formality and a long list of grievances. The Marlow hull peels away without a word. Take the castings back to Redwater Sound.

steps.text: Return the castings to Dill Harrow at Redwater Sound.

onComplete.text: Harrow stamps the papers, whichever house won, and says the feud will outlast the both of you. Whoever you sided with sends a House Rack, hand-numbered, to be fitted at the Redwater Sound outfitter. You are paid 4,000 cr.

missions.title: The Collector
missions.text: Ilsabet Voss collects things the way other people collect grudges, carefully and for life. She wants one case each of Halcyon Copperwine, Vesk Glowmoss and Stillwater Pearl, and she has heard you know the way to the Pearl's source. Her agent will meet you at each of the three places.
missions.acceptText: Voss hands you a list in violet ink and a purse for the first meeting. Her agent waits at Calder for the Copperwine, then at Vesk for the Glowmoss, and last at Skerry for the Pearl. When all three are handed over, come back to her at the Spires.

steps.text: Hand 4 t of Halcyon Copperwine to Voss's agent at Calder.

card.title: Voss's Agent
card.text: The agent is a patient man in a coat that cost more than his ship. He checks the seals on the crates, sniffs one bottle, and nods as if you had passed an examination.

choices.label: Hand over 4 t of Halcyon Copperwine

outcomes.text: The agent pays 3,000 cr from Voss's purse and writes you a receipt. He will wait next in Vesk, for the Glowmoss.

steps.text: Hand 3 t of Vesk Glowmoss to Voss's agent at Vesk.

card.title: Voss's Agent
card.text: The agent has acquired a lamp for the occasion, since the Glowmoss must be inspected in its own light. He holds it close and murmurs at it, which you decide not to take personally.

choices.label: Hand over 3 t of Vesk Glowmoss

outcomes.text: The agent pays 3,000 cr and tucks the Glowmoss out of the light. The last meeting is at Skerry, for the Pearl from Hushwater.

steps.text: Hand 2 t of Stillwater Pearl to Voss's agent at Skerry.

card.title: Voss's Agent
card.text: The agent has come to the rim in a heavier coat and a worse temper. He holds each Pearl to the light for exactly as long as it takes to be sure, and then a little longer.

choices.label: Hand over 2 t of Stillwater Pearl

outcomes.text: The agent pays 3,000 cr and says that is the set. Voss is waiting at the Spires in Quillon.

steps.text: Report to Ilsabet Voss at Quillon Spires.

onComplete.text: Voss looks over her agent's receipts, then at you, and smiles for the first time. She pays 5,000 cr and says the Cold Hold is yours to buy at the Spires outfitter. It keeps things exactly as they were, which is what she likes best in a hold.

missions.title: Echoes of the Long Patience
missions.text: Tobin Sarre tends the relay at Skerry Light and has the habit of listening to it when the bar is quiet. Since you took the Long Patience's log, the relay has been catching a faint repeating ping from Hushwater, always the same four notes. He would like a pilot who knows the old surveyor to go and hear it up close.
missions.acceptText: Sarre hands you a tuning fork, which he says is for luck and for nothing else. The lane to Hushwater runs from Skerry on the chart you already hold. Scan the source, then come back and tell him whether it is a ghost or a beacon.

steps.text: Fly to Hushwater and scan the survey echo.
Take what you heard back to Tobin Sarre at Skerry Light.

onComplete.text: The Long Patience's echo is a recorded survey log, looped until the power fails. It ends with a chart reference for somewhere past the lit edge, which nobody has yet been brave or bored enough to follow.
Sarre plays the recording through the relay, and the whole bar goes quiet for the four notes. He pays you 4,000 cr and says the surveyor was only ever waiting for someone to answer.

missions.title: The Doctor's Rounds
missions.text: Dr Ines Calloway has been making the rounds of the fringe ports for twenty years, and her ship has finally stopped agreeing to it. She has three lots of clinic crates and no way to deliver them on time. Late medicine is mostly just expensive luggage.
missions.acceptText: Calloway loads six tons of clinic crates, labelled in a hand you could read from orbit. First is Vesk Outpost, then Mirren Hollow, and last is Brackwater, back down the lane through Vesk and Lastlight. Each stop has its own deadline.

steps.text: Deliver the first clinic crates to Vesk Outpost within 6 days.
Deliver the second clinic crates to Mirren Hollow within 7 days.
Deliver the last clinic crates to Brackwater within 8 days.

onComplete.text: Dr Calloway says the fringe ports will remember a pilot who brings medicine on time, and forget one who brings it late. Both memories last a long while.
The last crate is signed for at Brackwater, and a stranger presses a hot mug into your hand without explanation. Calloway wires you 5,000 cr and a note saying her rounds are done for the season.

onFail.text: The crates are too late to matter. Calloway sends a short, kind note that makes you feel worse than a long angry one would have.

missions.title: The Last Lightkeeper
missions.text: Nell Ashgrove sells lamp-oil at Slagwater and keeps a map on her wall with a single pin in it. Before the lanterns went dark, one keeper in the Dimming refused to leave his post, and nobody has heard from him since. She would like to know whether he is still out there, and whether he needs anything.
missions.acceptText: Ashgrove sets a flask of lamp-oil on the counter, which she says is for the keeper and for no one else. His lantern hangs at Ebbing, one jump from Sootfall. After that, follow the lane on to Vane. Finish at Reed's Anchor, in Candlewick, where Ama Reed will want a name.

steps.text: Search Ebbing for the keeper's dead lantern.
Find the old keeper in Vane and talk to Perrin Vask.

card.title: Perrin Vask
card.text: Perrin Vask answers the channel on the third try, dry and unhurried. He kept his lantern lit for forty years and let it go dark only when its core was cut away. He is not angry about the Dimming. He is angry that no one has asked him what he saw.

choices.label: Offer him a berth to Reed's Anchor

outcomes.text: Vask laughs, short and surprised, and says the lamp-oil is welcome but the company is better. He will follow you in, at his own pace. Reed's Anchor is the place to tell his story.
You sit through forty years of lantern-keeping at the pace he chooses. He ends with a bearing for Reed's Anchor and a request that you tell it properly.

steps.text: Bring Perrin Vask's story to Reed's Anchor.

onComplete.text: Perrin Vask's account of the cut cores is now in Ama Reed's records, written in a keeper's hand.

Reed writes down every word Vask gave you, and lets him keep the pen. She pays you 3,000 cr and says the Keeper's Lens is yours to buy at the Reed's Anchor outfitter, where the Dimming can be seen properly.

missions.title: Lane Engineers
missions.text: Corrin has stopped wearing her warden's coat indoors, which you take to mean she is staying. The Concord has found three lane engineers willing to work in the Dimming, and nobody willing to fly them there. Reed's Anchor is the nearest place with a dock that will hold them.
missions.acceptText: The engineers climb aboard with toolrolls and the stoic look of people who were told it would be quiet. Corrin asks you to keep the cabin lit and the conversation dull. Reed's Anchor lies in Candlewick, deep inside the Dimming.

steps.text: Ferry the three lane engineers to Reed's Anchor.

onComplete.text: The engineers shoulder their kits and vanish into the Anchor's crowd without a backward glance. Reed's dockmaster hands you 6,000 cr from Corrin's purse.

missions.title: Lantern Cores
missions.text: The engineers have found the first dark lantern and have nothing to put in it. Corrin has six tons of new cores crated at Concordance, packed in straw with strict instructions. They need to reach Slagwater inside ten days, before the engineers run out of patience.
missions.acceptText: The cores are heavy, cold and faintly humming. Corrin makes you sign for each crate, then makes you sign for the straw. Slagwater, in Sootfall, will have a crew waiting.

steps.text: Deliver the lantern cores to Slagwater within 10 days.

onComplete.text: The Slagwater crew unpack the cores like newborns. Corrin's agent there pays you 7,000 cr and asks if you can stay for the lighting. You cannot, but you hear about it later.

missions.title: Three Lanterns
missions.text: With new cores in the old housings, three lanterns can be woken in turn. Corrin needs someone to fly past each one and scan it, so the engineers know it took. She suspects the Dimming will look different with a little light on it.
missions.acceptText: Corrin gives you a scanner key that opens a lantern housing without asking questions. Gloam, Pallow and Sootfall each have a lantern waiting. Take your time, and look up.

steps.text: Fly to Gloam and scan its relit lantern.
Fly to Pallow and scan its relit lantern.
Fly to Sootfall and scan its relit lantern.

onComplete.text: Three Dimming lanterns burn again. Settlers say the dark looks smaller from Gloam.
Three lanterns shine over the Dimming for the first time in years. Corrin sends 9,000 cr and a message that just says: look.

missions.title: Bram's Surrender
missions.text: The lanterns are relit, and Bram Kettle is still stripping the ones that are not. Corrin does not want him hurt. She wants him to stop, and she thinks he is tired enough to listen if someone approaches him as a person.
missions.acceptText: Corrin gives you terms signed in her own hand. If he refuses, she says, you will have to decide what to do with that. Bram works the dark lanterns in Sootfall.

steps.text: Find Bram Kettle in Sootfall and talk to him.

card.title: Bram Kettle
card.text: Bram Kettle listens with his arms folded, a man who has had the same argument with himself for months. His crew are tired of living off scraps, and he knows it. What he hears next will decide whether this ends quietly or loudly.

outcomes.text: Bram reads the terms twice, then once more aloud to his crew. They stand down without a shot. Corrin's agent pays you on the spot.

choices.label: Threaten him with a Concord fleet

outcomes.text: You frightened Bram Kettle into surrender. His crew will not forget it.
Bram goes pale, then nods, and his crew power down. It ends, but not kindly, and some of them will remember how. The Concord agent pays you on the spot.

onComplete.text: Corrin hears the news with her eyes closed. She says the charter can be signed now, and the 6,000 cr you were paid on the spot is yours to keep.

missions.combatLater: Bram's crew could fight instead of standing down, if the threat is made.

missions.title: The Charter
missions.text: The charter is a single sheet of paper, sealed in wax, with the Concord's name at the top and room for Ama Reed's at the bottom. Corrin has spent a month on the wording and a week on the wax. It has to be handed over in person, and carefully.
missions.acceptText: Corrin presses the charter case into your hands and tells you not to read it, then not to look like you are not reading it. Reed will be at her long table in Reed's Anchor. She will have opinions about the wax.

steps.text: Land at Reed's Anchor and put the charter in Ama Reed's hands.

onComplete.text: Ama Reed breaks the wax, reads for a long minute, and says it is a good wording. She pays you 6,000 cr and promises to arrive at Concordance in her own time.

missions.title: Escort the Liner
missions.text: Reed is coming to the ceremony, and the Concord is sending a liner to carry her and her people out of the Dimming. The route is still dark in places, and a liner cannot see as far as a scout. Corrin needs you to fly ahead and scan each system, so the liner knows the lane is clear.
missions.acceptText: A liner called the Constant Hour will sail from Reed's Anchor a day behind you, bound for the Oxbow lane. Scan Sootfall and Gloam ahead of her, then wait at Cairn Rest in Gloam, where she ends her leg. Corrin would like the trip to be entirely uneventful.

steps.text: Fly ahead to Sootfall and scan the lane for the liner.
Fly ahead to Gloam and scan the lane for the liner.
Land at Cairn Rest and wait for the liner to end her leg.

onComplete.text: The Constant Hour docks at Cairn Rest without a scratch, and Reed's delegation files off to change ships in their best coats. A Concord purser hands you 8,000 cr.

missions.title: The Ceremony
missions.text: The liner is ready and the delegation is on its way to Concordance. Corrin has one last thing to ask, and it is that you be there. She wants to put a face to the pilot who made all of this possible.
missions.acceptText: Corrin straightens her coat and will not say what is planned. Concordance is only a short hop away, and the ceremony begins when everyone is seated.

steps.text: Land at Concordance for the ceremony.

onComplete.text: Concordance yards will build you a Lantern-tender.
Corrin and Reed sign the charter side by side, and the whole hall applauds. The Concord pays you 10,000 cr, and its yards offer to build you a Lantern-tender.

missions.title: Lane Charts
missions.text: Tamsin Vey keeps the Free Reach's accounts in her head and its grievances in a ledger. The Reach has finally drawn its own lane charts, and she wants the independent traders to have them before anyone else tells them what the lanes are worth. Skerry Light is the nearest independent port that will read them in public.
missions.acceptText: Vey hands over two tons of rolled charts in oilcloth and asks you not to let anyone annotate them. Skerry Light is three jumps out, past Oxbow and Redwater.

steps.text: Deliver the lane charts to Skerry Light.

onComplete.text: The keepers of Skerry Light unroll the charts across the bar and argue about them happily until closing. A Reach factor pays you 6,000 cr and says the traders will remember who brought them.

missions.title: Settler Delegates
missions.text: Vey has come out to Cairn Rest herself, which for her is a long way from a podium. Four settler delegates from the Dimming want to speak at the Wrenhold compact, and they need passage out before the next meeting is called. Wrenhold is two jumps off, through Oxbow, and the meeting will not wait past twelve days.
missions.acceptText: The delegates file aboard with their papers in oilcloth and their best coats over their arms. They want to be at Wrenhold within twelve days, and not one of them has asked about the weather.

steps.text: Ferry the four settler delegates to Wrenhold within 12 days.

onComplete.text: The delegates step out into Wrenhold's loud public square and are immediately heckled, which they take as a welcome. Vey's clerk pays you 7,000 cr.

missions.title: Back-Pay
missions.text: Bram Kettle's salvagers have stripped the Dimming's dark lanterns for years because nobody else paid them to do anything else. Vey thinks they would sooner be paid by the Reach, and the compact wants their back-pay settled before Bram is asked for anything. He waits in Sootfall, and he will not be hurried.
missions.acceptText: Vey gives you terms written in a hand that could be mistaken for a lawyer's, and one piece of advice: let him talk first. Bram Kettle is somewhere in Sootfall, in the Dimming.

steps.text: Find Bram Kettle in Sootfall and settle his crew's back-pay.

card.title: Bram Kettle
card.text: Bram listens with his arms folded. His crew are owed a season's pay, and he says goodwill does not buy fuel. If the Reach wants his people, it can start by showing it can pay them.

outcomes.text: You put 4,000 cr on the table and the salvagers count it twice. Vey's factor is there within the hour, countersigns the receipt and repays your advance in full.

choices.label: Promise a share of the Reach's salvage

outcomes.text: Bram takes your promise as seriously as a promise deserves. His crew will wait for the compact to settle, and they will remember who asked them to.

onComplete.text: Bram sends word that his crew will hear the compact out. Vey pays you 8,000 cr and says the Reach pays its debts, in the end.

missions.title: Waylights
missions.text: The Reach wants its own lights in the Dimming, small and cheap and burning on Reach money, so its freighters can find the way. Vey has a case of waylight beacons already placed in three systems, and needs each one scanned to prove it took. Gloam, Pallow and Candlewick lie in a line down the lane from Oxbow.
missions.acceptText: Vey gives you a scanner key stamped with the Reach's three-ring mark. Start at Gloam and work in, past Pallow and on to Candlewick.

steps.text: Fly to Gloam and scan the Reach waylight.
Fly to Pallow and scan the Reach waylight.
Fly to Candlewick and scan the Reach waylight.

onComplete.text: Three Reach waylights now burn down the Dimming lane. Traders say they are small, and strangely cheerful.
Three small lights blink over the Dimming, in the Reach's colours. Vey pays you 9,000 cr and asks whether anyone objected.

missions.title: The Cordon
missions.text: A Concord patrol has closed the lane at Oxbow, and nobody in the Reach will say whether it is a customs check or a message. The delegates for the compact have to get through. Vey wants you to meet the patrol captain and choose how the Reach goes round her.
missions.acceptText: Vey spreads a chart on the table and puts her thumb on Oxbow. The captain commands the cordon in person. Two ways round are open to you, and one of them depends on whether you have been kind to the salvagers.

steps.text: Meet the Concord patrol captain at Oxbow.

card.title: Captain Davit Ruell
card.text: Captain Ruell is polite, immovable and visibly tired of it. She cannot let you through the cordon, but she can tell you which lanes she is not watching. Her patrol will hold whatever it holds.

choices.label: Take the long route round the cordon (costs fuel)

outcomes.text: You swing wide through the back lanes, burning fuel for days. The cordon never sees you, and Ruell's patrol is still holding its line when you clear it.

choices.label: Take the quiet route the salvagers know

outcomes.text: Bram's people owe you a favour, and they cash it. A salvager's pinnace guides you through a dead-lane gap the patrol has never mapped.

onComplete.text: You clear the cordon and report to Vey that the Concord is watching. She pays you 6,000 cr and says that is what she expected.

missions.combatLater: The Concord patrol could fight instead of letting the pilot go round.

missions.title: Bring Ama Reed
missions.text: Vey has taken a table at the end of Reed's Anchor's long hall and has not left it since breakfast. Ama Reed has agreed to speak for the Dimming at the Wrenhold compact, but only if somebody sensible takes her. Wrenhold is four jumps out, by Sootfall, Gloam and Oxbow.
missions.acceptText: Ama Reed boards with a small case and a large opinion of the lanes. She asks you to fly steadily and not to talk about the compact until Wrenhold.

steps.text: Ferry Ama Reed to Wrenhold.

onComplete.text: Ama Reed steps off at Wrenhold, takes in the square and the hecklers, and says she has had worse welcomes. Vey pays you 6,000 cr.

missions.title: The Signing
missions.text: The compact is ready, and so are the people it will bind. Vey has one last request, which is that you stand with them when it is signed. She wants it written down that a pilot was there.
missions.acceptText: Vey squares the paper on the table and will not say whether she is nervous. The signing is at Wrenhold, in the main hall, as soon as everyone is in their seat.

steps.text: Land at Wrenhold for the signing.

onComplete.text: The Wrenhold yards will fit you a Freewind runner.
Vey and Reed sign the compact, and the hall roars and heckles in the same breath. The Reach pays you 10,000 cr, and its yards offer to fit you a Freewind runner.
